quote: Beweise 1.) bei Zugrundelegung der Newtonschen Weltformel (Newton- sche Gravitation 2.) bei Zugrundelegung der Maxwellschen Elektricitäts- formel, dass wenn zur Zeit $t=-\infty$ (dies in geeigneter Weise definirt) Alles ruht, beständig Alles ruhen [-m-] bleiben muss d.h. Aus nichts kann nichts werden.
english: Prove, 1.) on the basis of the Newtonian world formula (Newtonian gravitation), 2.) on the basis of Maxwell's electricity formula, that if at time t = -infinity (suitably defined) everything is at rest, everything must remain at rest permanently, i.e. nothing can come from nothing.
topic: Hilbert proposes replacing boundary and interface conditions by extending the continuum over all space with rapidly varying coefficients, likewise for initial and end conditions in time; sets an exercise on Newtonian gravitation and Maxwell's equations that nothing comes from nothing; and defines a 'Griff' (grip) as a system of conditions fixing a single integral of a partial differential equation.

triage.modern_statement: Hilbert asks whether the laws of motion allow motion to begin out of total rest. Newtonian case: take the N-body equations m_i x_i'' = -∇_i U(x), with U = -Σ G m_i m_j/|x_i - x_j|. Suppose a solution is defined on (-∞, T] and is 'at rest at t = -∞', for example x_i'(t) → 0 (and perhaps the accelerations also → 0) as t → -∞. Must x_i' ≡ 0 for all time? Maxwell case: take the Maxwell equations with charges and currents. If the fields and sources are at rest (static, or zero) as t → -∞, must they stay that way? In modern terms this is a uniqueness/rigidity question for solutions fixed by asymptotic data at t = -∞ instead of ordinary Cauchy data. It is meant to illustrate his idea of replacing initial conditions with conditions at t = -∞. Everything turns on how 'suitably defined' is made precise, and Hilbert leaves that open.
triage.answered_by: I found no source that takes up Hilbert's exercise as such, and it is not among the 23 problems or the 24th problem. For the Newtonian case, the most natural reading (all velocities tend to zero as t → -∞) is in practice refuted by known results, though no source frames them as an answer to Hilbert. Chazy (1922) classified the final motions of the three-body problem, and parabolic motions are one of the classes. Maderna and Venturelli (Arch. Ration. Mech. Anal. 194, 2009) proved that collision-free parabolic solutions of the N-body problem exist from any initial configuration. Newton's equations are unchanged by time reversal, so reversing one of these solutions gives a non-trivial motion whose velocities tend to zero as t → -∞. My searches turned up nothing on the Maxwell case.

evidence.claim: Chazy classified the future and past final motions of the three-body problem in 1922. These final-motion classes are still a central topic in the study of the problem's long-term dynamics.

Maderna and Venturelli prove that for every initial configuration (and every minimizing normalized central configuration) there is a collision-free parabolic solution of the Newtonian N-body problem. 'Parabolic' here is the standard term for motions whose velocities tend to zero as t → ∞.
Publication details: Maderna and Venturelli, 'Globally minimizing parabolic motions in the Newtonian N-body problem', Arch. Ration. Mech. Anal. 194, 283–313 (2009).

triage.why: On the page this is a textbook-style exercise ('Beweise...'), used to illustrate replacing initial conditions with conditions at t = -∞. It is not a famous problem and I found no literature responding to it directly. In the Newtonian case, the naive reading (velocities → 0 as t → -∞) fails: time-reversed parabolic solutions are counterexamples, and these solutions are a topic of current research (Chazy's final motions; Maderna–Venturelli 2009 and later work). So the statement could only hold with a stronger definition of 'at rest at t = -∞', for example also requiring the bodies to stay a bounded distance apart, which Hilbert does not specify. Linking this to Hilbert is my own reasoning, not something the sources say. I found nothing on the Maxwell version. Because of these gaps, the verdict is 'possibly_unexplored' with low confidence, not 'solved'.
